claim: Every ideal a of A is contained in a maximal ideal.
suspected_error: The printed French omits the necessary condition a != A; the assertion is false for the unit ideal.
authority_locator: French canon source ega1/ega1-1-fr.tex lines 310-312; printed p.83 validation R6
evidence: The diplomatic French preserves the omission. The English discovery supplies a != A. The proof only applies to a nonempty closed complement V(a), which forces a to be proper.
proposed_disposition: Preserve the diplomatic French; add a != A in corrected French and source-aligned English with an explicit correction ledger entry.

claim: The quotient-spectrum identification is said to recover 1.1.12.
suspected_error: The uniquely applicable general quotient-spectrum result is 1.1.11; 1.1.12 concerns only reduction modulo the nilradical.
authority_locator: French canon source ega1/ega1-1-fr.tex lines 424-431; printed p.84 validation R7
evidence: The authority visibly prints 1.1.12. EGA I 1.1.11 identifies Spec(A/a) with V(a) for an arbitrary ideal and is exactly the result invoked here.
proposed_disposition: Preserve 1.1.12 in diplomatic French; use 1.1.11 in corrected French and source-aligned English with an explicit correction ledger entry.

claim: The proof identifies density by writing V(Ker phi)=X and referring to prime ideals and the nilradical of A.
suspected_error: For phi:A'->A the image lies in X'=Spec(A') and Ker(phi) is an ideal of A'; X and A must be X' and A' in these three proof references.
authority_locator: French canon source ega1/ega1-1-fr.tex lines 449-460; printed p.84 validation R7
evidence: The corollary correctly asks for density in X'. The closure formula is computed inside Spec(A'), so the subsequent ambient spectrum prime ideals and nilradical are those of A'.
proposed_disposition: Preserve the printed symbols in diplomatic French; repair all three linked symbols globally in corrected French and source-aligned English and record one atomic correction closure.

claim: After merely asserting that X is isomorphic to Spec(A), the text says that Gamma(X,O_X) is canonically identified with A.
suspected_error: The identification is canonical only relative to a chosen isomorphism X -> Spec(A), not from existence of a presentation alone.
authority_locator: French canon source ega1/ega1-1-fr.tex lines 1508-1515; printed p.96 validation R19
evidence: For A=k[t] and X=Spec(A), the identity presentation and the presentation induced by t -> t+1 give different identifications of global sections with A. Nearby arguments use the intrinsic ring Gamma(X,O_X), so no theorem depends on presentation independence.
proposed_disposition: Preserve diplomatic French; treat as lowest-severity editorial imprecision and if corrected layers clarify it say canonical after choosing X isomorphic to Spec(A), while defining A(X)=Gamma(X,O_X) intrinsically.

claim: All morphisms Spec(K) -> Spec(A), for A local with maximal ideal m and K a field, correspond to embeddings A/m -> K.
suspected_error: The statement omits the necessary restriction that the unique source point maps to the closed point m, equivalently that A -> K is local; a field-valued point may instead land at any prime of A.
authority_locator: French canon source ega1/ega1-2-fr.tex lines 441-449; printed p.102 validation R25 and diplomatic ledger FRENCH_DIPLOMATIC_TRANSCRIPTION_APPEND_P102_20260802.jsonl
evidence: Take A=k[t]_(t) and K=k(t). The inclusion A -> K defines Spec(K) -> Spec(A) with image the generic prime (0), so it does not factor through A/(t)=k. Stacks tag 01J6 classifies maps from spectra of local rings by an arbitrary image point and a local stalk map; the unlabelled points prose under section 01J5 gives the correct disjoint classification by pairs (p, kappa(p) -> K). EGA I 2.4.6 itself states this all-points formulation correctly.
proposed_disposition: Preserve the diplomatic French. In corrected French and English, restrict the sentence to morphisms whose image is the closed point, or replace the right-hand side by the disjoint union over p in Spec(A) of embeddings kappa(p) -> K; record the correction append-only and propagate it to every dependent statement.
